questions.question: How can technology create inequality in sport? Give specific examples.

points.text: Technology creates inequality because it is expensive and only available to well-funded teams and nations. For example, GPS tracking systems and performance analysis software cost thousands of pounds and are used by Premier League clubs but not by lower-league or grassroots teams. questions.question: Describe how VAR works in football and evaluate its impact on the game.

points.text: VAR (Video Assistant Referee) uses video technology to review four types of incident in football: goals, penalties, red cards and mistaken identity. The VAR team watches the game remotely and alerts the on-field referee to clear and obvious errors. The referee can then review the footage on a pitchside monitor or accept the VAR recommendation. questions.question: Why were full-body polyurethane swimming suits banned in 2010? What does this tell us about the relationship between technology and sport?

points.text: Full-body polyurethane swimming suits (e.g. LZR Racer by Speedo) were banned because they provided an unfair advantage through improved buoyancy and reduced drag. Over 40 world records were broken in 2009 alone, largely attributed to the suits rather than swimmer ability. This tells us that technology can go too far when it becomes the primary factor in performance rather than the athlete's skill

questions.question: Discuss the argument that technology is "ruining sport." Give points for and against.
